description:
Commit ddb474d6 changed enforce_key_usage to only reject intermediates whose KeyUsage extension is PRESENT but keyCertSign is NOT SET (Some(false)). Absent KeyUsage (None) now passes.

This behavior change is correct per RFC 5280 §6.1.4(n): 'If a KeyUsage extension is present, verify that the keyCertSign bit is set.'

However, there is no positive test that an intermediate with NO KeyUsage extension is accepted. The existing test key_usage_missing_cert_sign_returns_error only exercises the 'present but false' case.

The nca-int fixture has no KeyUsage but also has no BasicConstraints, so it fails NotCA before reaching the KeyUsage check — it cannot serve as a passing case.

If the logic were accidentally reverted to again reject absent KeyUsage, no test would catch the regression.

Fix: add a fixture for an intermediate CA with BasicConstraints cA=TRUE but no KeyUsage extension, and a positive test that validate_path accepts a chain through it.
title: pkix-path: missing positive regression test for absent KeyUsage extension passing validation
